title: Invocation stewardship mediator with progressive halts and structured-result gates
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: The Core API must support multi-tool chaining and function calling while streaming responses and preserving structured output contracts. Current orchestrator implementations are brittle when tools return large or partial outputs during streaming, and they don't reliably detect or mitigate recursive tool invocation loops. Goal: Implement an Invocation Stewardship Mediator (ISM) that manages tool call lifecycle for a single request: - orchestrate ordered multi-tool chains with explicit injection points into the stream - validate and gate structured tool results against schema contracts before committing to the streamed response - detect recursion/loops early with a bounded call-frame fingerprint and progressive halting policy - provide a backward-compatible compatibility layer so older SDKs/tool contracts continue to work without silent corruption - expose telemetry and per-request annotations for troubleshooting
acceptance_criteria: ISM routes multi-tool chains and preserves token-level streaming semantics (no rebuffering of previously emitted tokens)
Structured outputs from tools are validated against provided JSON-schema-like contracts; invalid results trigger sandboxed fallback behavior
Loop detection triggers a progressive halt when call-depth or repeated fingerprints exceed thresholds and emits a clear structured error to the client
Backward compatibility shim toggled by request header 'X-ISM-Compat: v1|v2' preserves old tool-result injection framing for v1 clients
Canary rollout shows <2% increase in p95 latency and fallback rate <0.5% after 2k requests sampled
End-to-end integration tests cover streaming+tool invocation, tool failure, partial streaming outputs, and recursion scenarios

comments: 2026-03-01 Aisha Patel: Kickoff — initial design doc posted to Confluence and prototype sketch for streaming markers. Decided to minimize rebuffering by injecting tool results as discrete structured chunks rather than rewriting previous tokens.

2026-03-03 Miguel Santos: Implemented preliminary call-frame fingerprint (rolling 64-bit hash of (tool_id + short-hash(params))) and added unit tests for simple recursion cases. Default max_depth=6. Observed a few false positives in nested map-reduce style orchestrations — need whitelist/parenting rules.

2026-03-05 Design Review (Aisha, Miguel, Luca): Agreed to add an explicit 'commit' marker for structured tool outputs so a tool can stream intermediate diagnostics without committing them to the public stream. This reduces accidental leakage of partial tool state.

2026-03-07 Eve (Runtime): Started sandboxed validator integration. Two design choices: fail-open (emit warning and continue) vs fail-closed (block commit and fallback). Proposal: fail-closed by default; allow tenant opt-in to fail-open for lower-latency experimental workloads.

2026-03-09 QA: Added fuzz harness that simulates streaming tool outputs with delayed 'commit' markers. Found a bug where cancellation of upstream stream didn't cancel in-flight tool tasks — added cancellation propagation to ISM's executor.

2026-03-10 Miguel Santos: Raised a PR with the call-frame detection and streaming markers. Needs performance review (kernel selection) and integration with batching layer. Seeking review from kernel/runtime team.
implementation_notes: Key runtime decisions: 1) Use a bounded LIFO call-frame fingerprint stack (max_depth configurable per-tenant). 2) On detection: emit structured 'recursion_detected' event in trace, then progressively halt: first offender => soft-fallback (drop the offending tool and continue), repeated => hard-fallback (abort chain and return structured error). 3) Structured output framing: tools emit chunked payloads with 'diagnostic' vs 'committed' flags; only 'committed' content is validated and forwarded to consumer. 4) Back-compat shim maps older tool-result inline markers into the new chunked commit model to avoid breaking older SDKs.
rollout_plan: Canary steps: 1% traffic for 48h -> evaluate p95 latency, error rate, fallback_rate. If stable, 5% for 24h, then 25% for 24h, then full. Rollback triggers: >5% increase in client-visible errors or p95 latency regression >10% absolute.
notes: Compatibility concerns: Some early adopters used tools that stream partial JSON fragments which were later reassembled by client-side logic. The commit-marker approach forces tool authors to choose when their fragments are considered authoritative. We need migration guides and a toggle for tenants during migration.
